# Rok Retar — Mobile Engineer

> Rok Retar is a Slovenian mobile engineer specializing in Android and Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP). He architected and executed a complete corporate migration transitioning production iOS systems to shared Kotlin codebases taken to production, keeping native UI where the platform earns it. This site is built natively in Kotlin with Kobweb. The following is an expanded description of each page for AI/LLM ingestion.

## Pages

### [Home](https://www.retar.app/)
The homepage introduces Rok Retar as an Android and Kotlin Multiplatform engineer from Slovenia. It outlines his philosophy: one Kotlin codebase, two platforms, native discipline intact. The page highlights his approach to KMP migrations — shared domain and data layers, native UI where the platform earns it — and lists four guiding principles. It also previews the Parrot case study and links to engineering notes.

### [Parrot — EPUB Reader & Audiobook Player](https://www.retar.app/parrot)
A case study for Parrot, a lightweight EPUB e-reader and audiobook player built as the companion app for Storyteller. Features include typography and text control, intuitive reading modes with page-flip navigation and fullscreen mode, e-ink display adaptation, background audio with notification controls, Read-Aloud sync with word-by-word highlighting, reading analytics, and a companion architecture. The page includes download links for the latest APK and a full version history with changelogs.

### [Building a Smooth, Infinite Carousel in Kobweb](https://www.retar.app/blog/infinite-carousel)
An engineering note on implementing a smooth, infinite carousel component in Kobweb using Compose for Web. Covers the technique for seamless looping, performance considerations, and the Compose-level API design.

### [Shipping SQLCipher inside a static Kotlin/Native framework](https://www.retar.app/blog/sqlcipher-static-kotlin-native-framework)
An engineering note on embedding SQLCipher into a static Kotlin/Native framework for iOS. Covers the build configuration, linking challenges, and how to ship encrypted SQLite in a KMP shared module that compiles to a static framework for iOS consumption.

## About

Rok Retar is a mobile engineer based in Slovenia. He engineers Android and Kotlin Multiplatform systems, including migrating a company's iOS app to shared Kotlin. The boundary is deliberate: shared business logic, shared data layers, shared domain models — with UI remaining native where it earns its keep. The domain layer never depends on data or UI; this is enforced by module structure.

Specializations:
- Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) migrations to production iOS
- Native Android architecture with Jetpack Compose
- Kobweb for Kotlin/WASM web development
- Software architecture with clean module boundaries
- SQLCipher and encrypted local storage in KMP

## Technology

This site is built natively in Kotlin with Kobweb, which brings a Compose-like developer experience to the web via Kotlin/WASM. Analytics are privacy-friendly via Umami (no cookies, no PII). No third-party trackers beyond Umami are used.
